Each control, pulse, and fine-step run contains 50,001 comparison times. \paragraph{Running the knee experiment.} From the repository root in a fresh MATLAB session with Simulink, run the commands below. They copy the saved library, knee model, and driver into a new temporary directory so that the driver can write its instrumented model and simulation results there. The argument \texttt{reader} selects the broadened ramps. The measurements above were reproduced in MATLAB R2025a Update~1. \begingroup\small\singlespacing \begin{verbatim} s = fullfile(pwd,"Code","Matlab","SNS_Simscape","results"); s = fullfile(s,"knee_transient_reflex_20261028"); b = fullfile(s,"original_snapshot"); w = tempname; d = fullfile(w,"demos"); p = fullfile(w,"results","knee"); mkdir(d); mkdir(p); copyfile(fullfile(b,"SNS_Library.slx"),w); copyfile(fullfile(b,"KneeReflexDemo.slx"),d); copyfile(fullfile(s,"run_transient.m"),p); addpath(p); run_transient(char("reader")); m = jsondecode(fileread(fullfile(p,"reader_summary.json"))); ref = jsondecode(fileread(fullfile(s,"replay_summary.json"))); isequaln(m,ref) \end{verbatim} \endgroup The last expression returns logical 1 for all fields in the expected JSON. In \path{reader_summary.json}, \path{paper_baseline_deg} is $-42.6392281008$, \path{paper_extension_excursion_deg} is $+1.0907928305$, \path{peak_latency_s} is $0.111$, \path{recovery_s} is $6.355$, and \path{step_error_deg} is $0.00005202734$, to the precision shown. The accompanying \path{reader_summary.mat} contains the common times and the nine signal columns for each condition. A fresh run reproduced every sample in the archived \path{replay_summary.mat}, including the angle, MN voltage, activation, and force traces used in the figure. \subsection{A Published Neural Mechanism as a Verification Target}\label{sec:rybak_verification} The reduced Python implementation of the two-level circuit of \citet{rybak_modelling_2006} passed 13 tests of drive dependence, repeatability, and phase after a motor deletion. Stimulation of the PF extensor population suppressed flexor motor output while the RG continued, and the flexor burst resumed at its expected phase. Stimulation of the RG extensor population also suppressed flexor output but shifted the subsequent rhythm. The two interventions distinguish a missing motor burst from a reset of the underlying clock in a neural-only model. The earlier \qty{5}{\second} knee trial compared startup in the graded circuit and its spiking twin. Its final-window measurements characterize startup activity. Section~\ref{sec:app_knee_transient} gives the settled pulse test and the inputs needed to reproduce it. \path{demos/sns_build_demo.m} and \path{demos/sns_build_beer_demo.m} (S) & Build the coupled knee and loaded-cup mechanisms. For the settled knee, use \path{run_transient.m} and the two saved model files named in Section~\ref{sec:app_knee_transient}. \\ M denotes \nolinkurl{Solid_Models/OpenSim/Gait2392_Robotbody/}, C denotes \nolinkurl{Code/MuJoCo_SNS/robot_torso/}, S denotes \nolinkurl{Code/Matlab/SNS_Simscape/}, and P denotes \nolinkurl{Code/MuJoCo_SNS/spinal/}. Subsequent bare filenames in a row use the directory of its first filename. The dissertation's \path{Defense/Session1_Handoff_20261104/} directory supplies portable configuration summaries and source paths for the newer experiments. Where it lists machine-local recordings or compiled models, full replay requires access to those files. The knee example in Section~\ref{sec:app_knee_transient} uses only the repository sources.

Earlier wording or anchor 135–184 \subsection{Layer-Specific Controls in the Reduced Deng Circuit}\label{sec:app_layer_stimulus} The fourteen-neuron Deng-derived implementation follows the circu… 135–184 \subsection{Layer-Specific Controls in the Reduced Deng Circuit}\label{sec:app_layer_stimulus} The fourteen-neuron Deng-derived implementation follows the circuit used in SNS-Toolbox demonstrations \citep{deng_neuromechanical_2019,nourse_sns_2023}. A \qty{0.1}{\milli\second} Euler step reproduced the existing neural integrator's complete \qty{24}{\second} baseline voltage trace exactly in the tested process. The baseline period was \qty{1.938}{\second}. Neural output drove the existing suspended, unilateral W2L mechanical model without afferent return. Hip commands came from the MN outputs; knee and ankle commands used the existing PF-to-activation mapping. This configuration tests transmitted circuit effects, not the original rat mechanics or bilateral walking. The initial sweep applied \qty{+2}{\nano\ampere} and \qty{+10}{\nano\ampere} to each layer for \qtylist{0.1;0.5}{\second}, together with two direct MN inhibitory controls. None met the deletion criterion. Subsequent stronger-current control series, including stimuli lasting two baseline periods (\qty{3.876}{\second}), retained the same circuit and mechanical parameters (Table~\ref{tab:layer_stimulus}). RG and PF stimuli began one-quarter cycle after a baseline RG onset; MN inhibition began \qty{0.05}{\second} into a baseline motor burst. Positive currents target the extensor RG or hip-PF population; negative currents target the hip-flexor MN. These currents are mechanistic controls, not experimentally calibrated physiological stimuli. A deletion required at least \qty{20}{\milli\second} of baseline motor activity in the stimulus window and suppression of at least half of that activity, using an activation threshold of 0.5. Phase residuals compare the final four recovered onsets with the nearest baseline onset, normalized by the baseline period. Residuals at or below 0.05 cycles were classified as non-resetting, and those at or above 0.15 as shifted; intermediate values remained indeterminate. RG and motor residuals were assessed separately. The two-cycle stimuli suppressed both expected flexor burst onsets at all three layers. Baseline and stimulated neural and mechanical trajectories were identical before stimulus onset. The \qty{1}{\second} PF pulse shifted the motor pattern without resetting the RG clock, whereas the two-cycle PF pulse preserved both schedules. The duration dependence cautions against treating every motor phase shift as an RG reset. The coupled mechanical traces contained large joint-limit violations, so these tests are interpreted through their neural responses in Table~\ref{tab:layer_stimulus}. \begin{table}[htbp] \centering\small \caption[Layer-specific stimulation controls]{Selected stronger-current controls in the reduced Deng-derived circuit. Phase residuals are fractions of the baseline cycle. ``No deletion'' means the specified suppression criterion was not met.} \label{tab:layer_stimulus} \begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}lrrcc>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}} \toprule Target & \unit{\nano\ampere} & \unit{\second} & RG phase & MN phase & Outcome \\ \midrule PF & $+50$ & 1.0 & 0.000 & 0.208 & Motor pattern shifted; RG preserved \\ RG & $+50$ & 3.876 & 0.211 & 0.211 & Resetting deletion \\ PF & $+50$ & 3.876 & 0.000 & 0.000 & Non-resetting deletion \\ MN & $-500$ & 3.876 & 0.000 & 0.000 & Non-resetting deletion \\ \bottomrule \end{tabularx} \end{table} \subsection{Archived AnimatLab Models}\label{sec:animatlab_validation} Headless reruns tested whether archived models reproduced their reference behavior in the original simulator. Eleven targetable rhythm and gait metrics passed their acceptance bands. The bilateral contact-driven model's rhythm generators had periods of \qtylist{0.450;0.467}{\second}; the modern W2L model showed joint oscillations at \qty{2.25}{\Hz}. The Li-model rerun reached \qty{0.637}{\meter\per\second} with step periods near \qty{1.3}{\second} \citep{li_bipedal_2017}. These are reference-model checks, not results for the combined Deng--Li model or evidence of unsupported walking. A separate MuJoCo translation of the Li controller and body did not reproduce that original-simulator walking result. In a \qty{20}{\second} ground test, mean forward speed was \qty{0.040}{\meter\per\second}, with eleven detected right-foot stance episodes and none on the left. The right-side period of \qty{1.294}{\second} alone therefore did not establish bilateral stepping. This failure distinguishes reproduction of the source model from successful transfer to another simulator. The original course-project circuit used a shared RG to supply bilateral PF and motor pathways. That source-model architecture for the motivating transfer attempt differs from the later W2L108 circuit, which has a separate RG on each side and additional sensory projections. The earlier instrumented AnimatLab trial records joint, neural, sensory, and body-motion channels over \qty{10}{\second} at a \qty{0.2}{\milli\second} interval. Figure~\ref{fig:animatlab_short_response} retains an aligned short window. Contact-sensory channels are membrane voltages, not contact forces. The initial external horizontal force and absence of a recorded timed vertical release prevent interpreting the run as an independent drop, touchdown, or stable-walking test. The reorganized bilateral project is a different configuration; its completion of simulation runs without sustained alternation is an assembly result. \begin{figure}[p] \centering \includegraphics[width=\textwidth,height=0.72\textheight,keepaspectratio]{animatlab_short_response_20261116.png} \caption[Archived AnimatLab neural and mechanical recording]{Aligned RG, PF, and MN activity and hip, knee, and ankle motion from the same suspended AnimatLab trial over \qtyrange{1}{2.5}{\second}. Extensor and flexor pathways are blue solid and orange dashed. Voltages are graded membrane signals, and the original joint conventions, including positive knee flexion, are retained. This is the earlier instrumented configuration.} \label{fig:animatlab_short_response} \end{figure} \section{Staged Calibration and Coupled-Model Experiments}\label{sec:sns_tuning_methods}\label{sec:sns_curriculum} Neural calibration and the physical curriculum test different requirements. Ordered neural fits evaluate intrinsic rhythm, timing with expected afferents, feedforward motor recruitment, and local-feedback refinement. Their activation targets are inverse-mechanics estimates from the reference motion, not measured electromyograms. A successful output fit is therefore followed by tests in the actual mechanical model. Each selected configuration retains its source hashes, settings, trial records, matched controls, and independent-process repeat. The physical curriculum separates deafferented air motion, afferented air motion, standing, supported stepping, and contact refinement; completing one stage does not establish the later stages.

Each selected configuration retains its source hashes, settings, trial records, matched controls, and independent-process repeat. The acceptance procedure first checks finite states, completion of the specified duration, anatomical knee bounds, and the required movement. Cadence, bilateral phase, loading, clearance, and assistance are then interpreted for that experiment. The historical gait score's reserved no-cycle value is $-25$; it must be rejected before ranking, since its numerical value exceeds many genuine movement scores. Scores from different configurations are not a common measure of locomotor quality. \subsection{BiW2Lvar+ Air Stages}\label{sec:app_biw2l_air} The revised graded BiW2Lvar+ controller completed both air stages with the same learned weights and a shared PF-to-MN expression scale of 0.1. The archived selector \texttt{hunt} is a compatibility identifier for this implementation; Hunt's contribution is the calibration method, not authorship of the controller. Table~\ref{tab:app_air_stages} reports the principal-cycle audit. The \qty{16}{\second} runs use the native MuJoCo biological-muscle formulation and the repaired Gait2392 human model. The retained adapter defines stage 1 with sensory return disabled and sustained normalized flexor and extensor commands set to zero. It defines stage 2 with live sensory return enabled and each command set to 0.15 on both sides, consistent with the fitted command manifest. That adapter also defines the same initialization seed for both stages, an added 0.4 on the right extensor and left flexor command channels for the first 50 neural calls (\qty{100}{\milli\second}); this seed does not impose a continuing stride clock. It clamps the postural, balance, and functional-command channels off, sets direct tonic RG current to zero, and disables the legacy shared-drive input. The original launch adapter and complete consumed-command traces were not recovered; these are declared adapter settings rather than independently verified input samples from that launch. Thus these air stages cannot be treated as a matched feedback-only comparison. The retained shared descending drive in the separate historical weaning study below belongs to a different configuration. \begin{table}[htbp] \centering\small \caption[Fixed-controller air-stage evaluations]{BiW2Lvar+ air stages using unchanged learned weights. Principal cycles, periods, and phase errors are evaluated over $5\leq t<14$\,s of each \qty{16}{\second} trial. Phase error is distance from bilateral antiphase in cycles. Negative knee angles indicate flexion. Sensory return and sustained commands both differ between stages.} \label{tab:app_air_stages} \begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}Xrrrr@{}} \toprule Condition & Cycles R/L & Period (s) & Phase error & \shortstack{Maximum knee angle\\R/L (deg)} \\ \midrule Deafferented air & 4/4 & 2.466 & 0.0337 & $-1.300/-1.326$ \\ Afferented air & 7/7 & 1.300 & 0.0933 & $-1.718/-1.801$ \\ \bottomrule \end{tabularx} \end{table} The original stage-1 counter counted secondary flexion humps as additional cycles. The preserved principal-cycle audit instead uses autocorrelation and separated principal peaks; its checks accept antiphase double-hump signals and reject synchronous, frozen, and fast test signals. The legacy failed assessment remains in the record. Stage 2 passes both counters. Secondary humps remain a waveform-quality limitation, even when the principal-motion criterion passes. Ground contact is disabled and measured foot forces are zero. The adopted stage-2 suspension statistic is \qty{99.860}{\percent}, calculated from \qty{768.662}{\newton} mean spring force over \qtyrange{5}{16}{\second} using the legacy total model mass of \qty{78.4646}{\kilogram} and weight of \qty{769.737726}{\newton}. That mass includes a separate fixed \qty{0.1}{\kilogram} ground body. The aligned-recording metadata instead uses the pelvis subtree, \qty{78.3646}{\kilogram} or \qty{768.756726}{\newton}; dividing the same legacy force samples by that denominator gives \qty{99.9877}{\percent}. The adopted percentage is retained with its original denominator. Figure~\ref{fig:sns_biw2l_air} displays unnormalized force in newtons. The legacy samples are tagged at interval start, while aligned states are tagged at interval end, so an independently selected aligned window must also retain its own timestamps. These measures characterize suspension, with frontal guidance retained, rather than a minimum ground-walking support requirement. Higher-expression trials stopped at the predictive knee-extension guard; the completed condition retains the guard and does not clip joint state. This controller has not completed standing or ground stages.

Score comparisons below use the same configuration and analysis window. \subsection{BiW2Lvar+ Air Stages}\label{sec:app_biw2l_air} The revised graded BiW2Lvar+ controller completed two \qty{16}{\second} air trials on the repaired Gait2392 human model with native MuJoCo biological muscles. The trials share learned weights and a PF-to-MN expression scale of 0.1. The software selector \texttt{hunt} identifies this implementation in the records. Hunt supplied the calibration method. Table~\ref{tab:app_air_stages} gives the principal knee-flexion peaks and the intervals from which the periods were measured. The retained adapter and fitted command settings specify zero sustained flexor and extensor command in stage 1 and normalized command 0.15 to all four channels in stage 2. The same startup signal adds 0.4 to right extensor and left flexor commands for the first 50 neural updates (\qty{100}{\milli\second}). The adapter suppresses postural, balance, and functional commands and sets the direct tonic RG and legacy shared-drive inputs to zero. Sensory return is disabled in stage 1 and enabled in stage 2. Both sustained command and sensory return therefore change together. The original launch adapter and the complete consumed command stream are unavailable. These settings describe the compatible retained implementation. In that adapter, group Ia receives signed path velocity divided by \qty{0.6}{\meter\per\second}, and group II receives signed path-length deviation from its fitted midpoint divided by its fitted half-range. Both normalized inputs are clipped to $[-1,1]$ before current gain is applied. For each muscle, group Ib receives positive tension $\max(-F_{\rm actuator},0)$ divided by its maximum force and multiplied by the Ib gain. The central load input separately scales summed ipsilateral antigravity-muscle tension by its reference target force. These are modeled musculotendon signals. The generic Gait2392 runner also uses Ia, II, and Ib labels but applies rectification to lengthening and includes a phase-dependent tonic term in II. \begin{table}[htbp] \centering\small \caption[Fixed-controller air-stage evaluations]{BiW2Lvar+ with unchanged learned weights. Principal knee-flexion peaks, median interpeak period, and distance from bilateral antiphase are measured over $5\leq t<14$\,s of each \qty{16}{\second} trial. Four and seven peaks yield three and six complete interpeak intervals per side, respectively. The last column gives the maximum whole-trial native angle. Negative values indicate flexion.} \label{tab:app_air_stages} \begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}Xrrrr@{}} \toprule Condition & \shortstack{Principal knee\\peaks R/L} & Period (s) & \shortstack{Phase error\\(cycles)} & \shortstack{Maximum knee\\R/L (deg)} \\ \midrule Deafferented air & 4/4 & 2.466 & 0.0337 & $-1.300/-1.326$ \\ Afferented air & 7/7 & 1.300 & 0.0933 & $-1.718/-1.801$ \\ \bottomrule \end{tabularx} \end{table} The original stage-1 counter also detected small secondary flexion humps. The revised measurement uses autocorrelation to estimate cadence and then selects separated principal peaks. It accepts an antiphase double-hump test signal and rejects synchronous, frozen, and fast signals. Stage 1 failed the original count, whereas stage 2 passed both methods. The secondary humps remain visible in the stage-1 waveform. With ground contact disabled, both feet recorded zero force. The stage-2 suspension spring supplied a mean \qty{768.662}{\newton} over $5\leq t<16$\,s. The interval-start samples end at \qty{15.998}{\second}. Mean support was \qty{99.860}{\percent} of the original denominator, \qty{769.737726}{\newton} from \qty{78.4646}{\kilogram}, which includes a fixed \qty{0.1}{\kilogram} ground body. Dividing the same mean force by the moving pelvis-subtree weight, \qty{768.756726}{\newton} from \qty{78.3646}{\kilogram}, gives \qty{99.9877}{\percent}. Figure~\ref{fig:sns_biw2l_air} shows force in newtons with the aligned states, which use interval-end timestamps. This apparatus isolates suspended limb motion and retains frontal guidance. Higher PF-to-MN expression triggered the predictive knee-extension stop. The reported configuration completed the air stages with that guard and without clipping joint state. Standing and ground stepping remain unverified for this controller.

Earlier wording or anchor 212–267 \subsection{Fixed-Weight Neural Noise and Phase-Specific Stimuli}\label{sec:app_current_noise}\label{sec:app_biw2l_stimulus} With the stage-2 weights fixed, ind… 212–267 \subsection{Fixed-Weight Neural Noise and Phase-Specific Stimuli}\label{sec:app_current_noise}\label{sec:app_biw2l_stimulus} With the stage-2 weights fixed, independent ongoing current noise was applied to four RG cells. Three seeds were evaluated at each stationary standard deviation of \qtylist{0.01;0.025}{\nano\ampere}, with a \qty{20}{\milli\second} correlation time. All six noisy trials completed and retained the principal-motion, knee, and frontal-separation criteria. A zero-noise control and repeated noisy seed also passed. The repeated seed reproduced joint states, neural voltages, and applied noise exactly in a fresh process. This tests the selected air condition under continuous neural-current disturbance; it is distinct from perturbing fixed connection parameters or testing ground balance. Matched baseline and stimulus runs applied \qty{2}{\nano\ampere}, \qty{100}{\milli\second} pulses separately to the right RG-F, right hip-flexor PF, and right iliacus MN, together with a \qty{-2}{\nano\ampere} right PF control. The silent-phase series begins at \qty{7.10}{\second}, and the active-phase series at \qty{7.65}{\second}. Pre-pulse neural trajectories agree exactly. The silent-phase PF pulse reaches only \qty{-3.058}{\milli\volt}, below the outgoing ramp's \qty{0}{\milli\volt} onset; transmission saturates at \qty{5}{\milli\volt}. Its MN difference is below \qty{6e-8}{\milli\volt}. During the active phase, the excitatory PF pulse changes PF voltage by up to \qty{1.14}{\milli\volt} and right iliacus MN voltage by \qty{0.16}{\milli\volt}. The active-phase direct MN pulse changes its voltage by \qty{1.79}{\milli\volt} and subsequently right RG-F voltage by \qty{6.04}{\milli\volt} through the closed neural--mechanical loop. Each maximum is the absolute paired difference over the interval from onset, inclusive, to \qty{3.4}{\second} after onset, exclusive: \qtyrange{7.10}{10.50}{\second} for the silent series and \qtyrange{7.65}{11.05}{\second} for the active series, with the upper endpoint excluded. These experiments distinguish rhythm generation, progression, and bilateral contact coordination, rather than treating them as interchangeable outcomes. \subsection{CAD Robot: Contact Handover and Supported Clearance}\label{sec:app_cad_supported_stance} The CAD-derived model retains its four-bar knees and spherical hips, using the anatomical frame $x$ anterior, $y$ superior, and $z$ right. The selected controller has 262 graded cells, 230 inputs, and 54 reference-tension actuators. RG activity supplies timing, while an engineering force allocator supplies posture, stance-load, and clearance targets to the MN layer. MN target-current compensation limits normal PF/reflex authority over those outputs. The model therefore evaluates this hybrid architecture, not a complete unmodified neural controller with calibrated dynamic BPA forces. The selected condition completed \qty{28}{\second}. During $16\leq t<28$\,s, mean vertical harness force was \qty{570.20625}{\newton}, or \qty{77.5}{\percent} of the \qty{735.75}{\newton} weight of the \qty{75}{\kilogram} model. Seven right and six left qualifying unloaded-clear intervals produced twelve alternations. Each interval required whole-foot mesh clearance above \qty{5}{\milli\meter}, ipsilateral normal load below \qty{7.36}{\newton}, contralateral load above \qty{15}{\newton}, and duration of at least \qty{80}{\milli\second}. The retained every-\qty{2}{\milli\second} knee-bound accumulator reports whole-trial minimum flexion of \ang{11.20} on the right and \ang{5.10} on the left, against a \ang{1} guard. The saved \qty{10}{\milli\second} traces are a different sampling interval and do not independently reconstruct every physics-step extremum. The \qty{-74.7}{\milli\meter} world-forward displacement describes guided stepping approximately in place. Orientation and lateral guidance remained active. \begin{figure}[p] \centering \includegraphics[width=14cm]{CAD_supported_traces_20261116.pdf} \caption[Quantitative supported CAD stepping]{CAD signals during $16\leq t<28$\,s: RG flexor-minus-extensor voltage (A), native flexion-negative knees (B), foot normal loads (C), and whole-foot mesh heights (D). With $u=\operatorname{clip}[(F-F_0)/(F_1-F_0),0,1]$, confidence is $c=u^2(3-2u)$, using nominal thresholds $F_0=\qty{1}{\newton}$ and $F_1=\qty{5}{\newton}$. This verifies execution of that reference stack; it does not validate transfer to Gait2392 or establish physiological validity. An exploratory adaptation reproduced its corrected Python equations in a compiled implementation within $3.34\times10^{-16}$ over 2000 steps. Nevertheless, its 960-trial duration-and-speed search selected a tumbling trajectory, which was rejected as walking. Equation agreement did not establish transfer of the source controller's locomotion. The native baseline and rejected adaptation are distinct results: reproducing the original stack supplies a reference for transfer, while the unsuccessful search remains rejected as walking. \section{Spiking-Neuron Comparisons}\label{sec:spiking_methods}\label{sec:spiking_results}\label{sec:disc_spiking} The spiking variants replace afferent, rhythm-generator, and interneuron populations while retaining graded motor neurons. Synapses onto motor neurons are calibrated by mean conductance, preserving the continuous activation interface. This construction does not require the network dynamics or resulting movement to remain unchanged. Calibration and full conversion tables are in Appendix~\ref{app:neuron_equations}. Action potentials introduce voltage fluctuations absent from a graded signal, so raw membrane-voltage variability is not an equivalent measure of controller output. Figure~\ref{fig:spike_ground} compares filtered neural readouts, muscle activation, and joint motion under the same drive, support, and selected parameters. For a hardware comparison using pulse-width modulation (PWM), both signals would need to pass through the same command encoder and valve limits. \subsection{MuJoCo Network and Ground Evaluation} Under constant drive, the non-spiking and spiking rhythm periods were \qtylist{0.399;0.621}{\second}, respectively. The spiking period is \qty{55.6}{\percent} longer. Timing agreement therefore requires more than copying the selected parameters. The historical untuned spiking variant produced bilateral cycling in a supported ground evaluation where the non-spiking winner cycled predominantly on one side (Table~\ref{tab:spike_ground}; Figure~\ref{fig:spike_ground}). Proposed wording or action 434–479 \section{Execution, Provenance, and Reproduction Tools}\label{sec:app_execution_provenance} I timed one complete Gait2392 process per backend for the 1,025-cell… 434–479 \section{Execution, Provenance, and Reproduction Tools}\label{sec:app_execution_provenance} I timed one complete Gait2392 process per backend for the 1,025-cell source configuration selected by \texttt{hunt}. Its \qty{16}{\second} stage-1 protocol included \qty{0.6}{\second} of held-pose preparation and \qty{15.4}{\second} on the physics clock. Elapsed process time was \qty{199.624}{\second} with native SNS and \qty{29.284}{\second} with the sparse backend, a 6.82-fold speedup. Within those processes, accumulated neural-call time was \qty{179.079}{\second} and \qty{9.780}{\second}, an 18.31-fold speedup. All 45 captured numerical arrays and the compiled-model hash agreed. I next compared compact and sparse implementations of the 1,033-cell Hunt-PT+RC circuit. After a separate 1,200-step state-agreement check in each family, the median of three 3,000-update warm neural-kernel timings was \qty{0.8953}{\second} for sparse and \qty{0.5551}{\second} for compact, a factor of 1.613. In one paired \qty{16}{\second} stage-4 diagnostic, evaluator time fell from \qty{92.944}{\second} to \qty{91.516}{\second}, a factor of 1.016. That interval included simulation, capture, and assessment, excluding imports, pre-run setup, and final serialization. All 62 numerical arrays and compiled-model hashes agreed. The backend preserves summation order. Spiking and electrical channels continue to use their existing implementations. In the bilateral-RG W2L circuit with Ib input ports, the ratio was 1.425 for one warm block of 10,000 neural updates per backend following 5,000 state-comparison steps. The paired \qty{30}{\second} body trajectories agreed exactly. This measurement times the isolated W2L neural updates. Only the first Gait2392 comparison above timed the complete process externally. Table~\ref{tab:app_script_map} gives the executable sources. Section~\ref{sec:app_knee_transient} includes a complete run from two portable model files and compares the output with the expected JSON. For the newer coupled experiments, the available records vary by test. The noise and pulse runs include the applied currents and aligned states. For BiW2Lvar+, the archived launch adapter and full consumed command stream are unavailable (Section~\ref{sec:app_biw2l_air}). Proposed wording or action \begin{samepage} For example, a researcher may ask whether type Ia feedback excites the muscle from which it originates or inhibits its antagonist. SADb contains separate… \begin{samepage} For example, a researcher may ask whether type Ia feedback excites the muscle from which it originates or inhibits its antagonist. SADb contains separate pathway records for ``Ia monosynaptic excitation'' and ``Ia inhibitory.'' These describe complementary connections: direct excitation of the agonist motor pool and inhibition of an antagonist through an inhibitory interneuron. The researcher can inspect the linked studies and model records to compare their target muscles, intervening neurons, and task conditions before choosing how to implement the sensory afferent pathways. The afferent class alone does not specify the sign of every connection.\par \end{samepage}

Earlier wording or anchor Robotic tests can also return predictions to biology. \citet{ijspeert_swimming_2007} implemented a spinal-cord model in a salamander robot that switched between walking a… Robotic tests can also return predictions to biology. \citet{ijspeert_swimming_2007} implemented a spinal-cord model in a salamander robot that switched between walking and swimming as control drive changed. The model predicted lower intrinsic frequencies for limb oscillators than for body oscillators, and the authors presented biological data supporting that prediction. This exchange illustrates the broader motivation for the humanoid project: biological evidence informs a controllable model, whose behavior can generate questions for subsequent biological experiments.

Proposed wording or action For each site, domain coverage is estimated from the saved grid by \begin{equation} C=100\,\frac{\sum_{i,j} w_iw_j D_{ij}M_{ij}}{\sum_{i,j}w_iw_jD_{ij}}, \label{eq:angul… For each site, domain coverage is estimated from the saved grid by \begin{equation} C=100\,\frac{\sum_{i,j} w_iw_j D_{ij}M_{ij}}{\sum_{i,j}w_iw_jD_{ij}}, \label{eq:angular_domain_coverage} \end{equation} where $D_{ij}$ indicates inclusion in the evaluated domain and $M_{ij}$ indicates that the human torque requirement is met. On each uniformly spaced axis, trapezoidal weights are one-half at the outer endpoints and one at interior samples; the common angular increments cancel in the ratio. Active-force coverage uses the positive-tension indicator in place of $M_{ij}$. For single-DoF routes, this becomes interval coverage; the repeated fixed coordinate cancels. These are grid-based quadrature estimates, rather than exact continuous-domain boundaries. Each site's fraction is normalized before the equal-site mean is calculated.

The RG intervention shifts subsequent timing, whereas the displayed PF and MN interventions preserve the RG schedule.} \label{fig:layer_stimulus_validation} \end{figure} \FloatBarrier \subsection{Archived AnimatLab Models}\label{sec:animatlab_validation} Headless reruns tested whether archived models reproduced their reference behavior in the original simulator. Eleven targetable rhythm and gait metrics passed their acceptance bands. The bilateral contact-driven model's rhythm generators had periods of \qty{0.450}{} and \qty{0.467}{\second}; the modern W2L model showed joint oscillations at \qty{2.25}{\Hz}. The Li-model rerun reached \qty{0.637}{\meter\per\second} with step periods near \qty{1.3}{\second} \citep{li_bipedal_2017}. These are reference-model checks, not results for the combined Deng--Li model or evidence of unsupported walking. A separate MuJoCo translation of the Li controller and body did not reproduce that original-simulator walking result. In a 20-second ground test, mean forward speed was \qty{0.040}{\meter\per\second}, with eleven detected right-foot stance episodes and none on the left. The right-side period of \qty{1.294}{\second} alone therefore did not establish bilateral stepping. This failure distinguishes reproduction of the source model from successful transfer to another simulator. \section{Tuning and Supported Evaluations}\label{sec:sns_tuning_methods}\label{sec:sns_curriculum} Free network gains were searched with a tree-structured Parzen estimator, with each candidate evaluated through simulation. The staged procedure separates suspended rhythm generation, sensory feedback, standing, and ground evaluations (Table~\ref{tab:sns_curriculum}). Finalists were checked under \qty{1}{\percent} multiplicative parameter perturbations and changes in drive. Such checks probe the neighborhood of a selected configuration; they do not establish robustness to untested loads or removal of the harness. The cycle-shape metric assigns zero to perfect agreement. A run without detectable cycles returns $-25$ as a reserved failure value. Because this value is numerically greater than the genuine-gait scores below, failed runs must be identified before ranking scores. That value itself is not a valid measure of gait quality. The curriculum is shown in Table~\ref{tab:sns_curriculum} in Chapter~\ref{ch:sns}. \subsection{Reference-Library Comparison}\label{sec:gait_library_results} The 43-cycle library contains 32 running trials from eight subjects at four speeds, ten walking references, and a predicted-walking cycle. The walking references span prescribed speeds of \qtyrange{0.5}{2.0}{\meter\per\second} and self-selected trials. The production network (\texttt{s3k}), reduced-connection network (\texttt{s3kpruned}), six-group activation network (\texttt{syn6}), and W2L-organization network (\texttt{w2lvar}) were scored without treating a good tuning-reference score as evidence of generalization. Library scores were substantially more negative (Table~\ref{tab:gait_sweep}), and the evaluations showed unilateral or asymmetric gait. This comparison bounds transfer to the available references; it does not validate normal human walking. Table~\ref{tab:gait_sweep} uses the production pipeline's cycle-shape kinematic score. The tuning-reference column reports each configuration on its tuning reference; the library mean averages that score over all 43 reference cycles. \begin{table}[htbp] \caption{Four controller configurations evaluated on their tuning reference and the 43-cycle reference library. For genuine gait cycles, larger kinematic scores indicate closer agreement; zero is perfect agreement.} \label{tab:gait_sweep} \begin{tabular}{@{}lrrl@{}} \toprule & \textbf{Tuning-ref.} & \textbf{Library mean} & \textbf{Most negative reference} \\ & \textbf{score} & \textbf{score (43 refs)} & \textbf{(score)} \\ \midrule \texttt{s3k} & $-186.4$ & $-8776$ & \texttt{Case\_40\_motion} ($-8841$) \\ \texttt{s3kpruned} & $-176.1$ & $-6924$ & \texttt{Case\_40\_motion} ($-6986$) \\ \texttt{syn6} & $-200.4$ & $-9961$ & \texttt{Case\_40\_motion} ($-10040$) \\ \texttt{w2lvar} & $-144.5$ & $-5808$ & \texttt{subject08\_Run\_20002} ($-5896$) \\ \bottomrule \end{tabular} \end{table} \subsection{Direct Kinematics Overlay}\label{sec:app_ik_overlay} The saved human-model controller reproduced its cycle-shape score of $-145.07$ in an independent process. The direct overlay in Figure~\ref{fig:gait2392_ik_overlay} uses the Gait2392 walking inverse-kinematics trajectory and its paired ground-reaction-force file. Model cycles begin when vertical foot loading crosses \qty{50}{\newton}; reference stance is defined using the same force threshold. Ten cycles per side, with durations between 0.35 and 2.5 seconds, were retained using the existing cycle detector. Each leg was aligned to its own onset and resampled over the gait cycle, without fitting phase, subtracting the mean angle, or scaling amplitude. Mean cycle periods were \qty{1.285}{\second} on the right and \qty{1.254}{\second} on the left, compared with \qty{1.233}{\second} and \qty{1.213}{\second} in the reference. Model stance fractions were 0.710 and 0.649, compared with 0.610 in the reference. Table~\ref{tab:ik_absolute_rmse} reports absolute-angle errors between mean cycles. These errors retain posture offsets and are distinct from the mean-removed cycle-shape errors used in tuning. The hip and knee mismatches show why cycle counts and a scalar score must be accompanied by the trajectories and contact timing. \begin{table}[htbp] \centering \caption[Absolute-angle errors against Gait2392 inverse kinematics]{Unshifted absolute-angle RMSE between mean model and reference cycles, in degrees.} \label{tab:ik_absolute_rmse} \begin{tabular}{lrr} \toprule Joint & Right & Left \\ \midrule Hip & 28.03 & 24.65 \\ Knee & 27.44 & 28.45 \\ Ankle & 8.71 & 7.38 \\ \bottomrule \end{tabular} \end{table} \subsection{Pathway-Removal Tests}\label{sec:walker_variant_results} Individual pathway classes were removed from each selected configuration and the model re-evaluated on its tuning reference (Table~\ref{tab:walker_ablations}). Removing Ia feedback from the production configuration eliminated detected cycles. Other removals changed the score without necessarily eliminating movement. The different response of the six-synergy variant shows that these dependencies belong to the tested network configurations, rather than constituting a general claim about biological necessity. The systematic pattern-formation and motoneuron stimulation series for these full Gait2392 networks was not completed. The reduced-circuit tests in Section~\ref{sec:app_layer_stimulus} address a separate, smaller model. \begin{table}[htbp] \caption{Pathway-removal tests on the tuning reference. Full-model rows give unchanged baselines. A score of $-25$ is the fixed no-cycle fallback and denotes failure, despite exceeding the genuine-gait scores.} \label{tab:walker_ablations} \small\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.20\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.24\textwidth}@{}} \toprule \textbf{Configuration} & \textbf{Removed pathway} & \textbf{Score} \\ \midrule \texttt{s3k} (full model) & none & $-186.4$ \\ & Ia afferents & $-25$ (no cycles detected) \\ & all afferent classes & $-267.8$ \\ & Renshaw cells & $-267.3$ \\ & group-II afferents & $-255.2$ \\ & Ib afferents & $-180.3$ \\ & contact channels & $-183.9$ \\ & interleg commissural pathways & $-174.9$ \\ \addlinespace \texttt{syn6} (full model) & none & $-200.4$ \\ & all afferent classes & $-190.5$ \\ \addlinespace \texttt{w2lvar} (full model) & none & $-144.5$ \\ & Ia afferents & $-273.5$ \\ & weak rhythm-generator mutual excitation & $-279.9$ \\ & Renshaw cells & $-142.4$ \\ \bottomrule \end{tabularx} \end{table} \section{Spiking-Neuron Comparisons}\label{sec:spiking_methods}\label{sec:spiking_results}\label{sec:disc_spiking} The spiking variants replace afferent, rhythm-generator, and interneuron populations while retaining graded motor neurons. Synapses onto motor neurons are calibrated by mean conductance, preserving the continuous activation interface. This construction does not require the network dynamics or resulting movement to remain unchanged. Calibration and full conversion tables are in Appendix~\ref{app:neuron_equations}. \subsection{MuJoCo Network and Ground Evaluation} Under constant drive, the non-spiking and spiking rhythm periods were \qty{0.399}{} and \qty{0.621}{\second}, respectively (Figure~\ref{fig:spike_rhythm}). The spiking period is \qty{55.6}{\percent} longer. Timing agreement therefore requires more than copying the selected parameters. The untuned spiking variant produced bilateral cycling in a ground evaluation where the non-spiking winner cycled predominantly on one side (Table~\ref{tab:spike_ground}; Figure~\ref{fig:spike_ground}). This individual comparison motivates further controlled testing; it does not establish superiority of spiking control. \begin{figure}[htbp] \centering \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{spiking_mirror_rhythm.pdf} % ALT TEXT: see spiking_mirror_rhythm_alt.txt beside the figure file. \caption[Constant-drive rhythm, non-spiking versus spiking]{Constant-drive rhythm in the non-spiking network (A) and spiking variant (B). The observed periods are \qty{0.399}{} and \qty{0.621}{\second}; the latter is \qty{55.6}{\percent} longer. The panels use different neural readouts: graded population difference versus individual spiking cells.} \label{fig:spike_rhythm} \end{figure} \begin{table}[htbp] \caption{Supported ground evaluation at the same selected parameters (16 s), with no spiking re-tuning. Knee minima and contact duty are computed over detected cycles. The kinematic score is a cycle-shape error metric: zero denotes perfect agreement, and less negative scores indicate closer agreement.} \label{tab:spike_ground} \begin{tabular}{@{}lcc@{}} \toprule \textbf{Metric} & \textbf{Non-spiking winner} & \textbf{Spiking mirror (untuned)} \\ \midrule Kinematic score & $-161.57$ & $-236.35$ \\ Gait cycles, right / left & 9 / 0 (left frozen) & 8 / 9 (bilateral) \\ Cycle knee minimum & \ang{-64.3} & \ang{-79.8} \\ Contact duty, right / left & 0.637 / 0.985 & 0.799 / 0.856 \\ Maximum pelvis tilt & \ang{22.1} & \ang{19.2} \\ Non-finite states / fell & no / up & no / up \\ \bottomrule \end{tabular} \end{table} \begin{figure}[htbp] \centering \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{spiking_mirror_ground_gait.pdf} % ALT TEXT: see spiking_mirror_ground_gait_alt.txt beside the figure file. \caption[Ground gait, non-spiking winner versus untuned spiking mirror]{Ground-evaluation joint angles at the non-spiking winner parameters. The non-spiking model cycles predominantly on the right (A, C), while the untuned spiking variant cycles both legs (B, D). Solid indigo denotes left, and dashed orange right. Both use the supported evaluation protocol.} \label{fig:spike_ground} \end{figure} \subsection{Simulink Demonstrations} The graded and spiking knee-reflex demonstrations were compared over matched \qty{5}{\second} runs (Table~\ref{tab:spike_knee}; Figure~\ref{fig:spike_knee}). The beverage example retained approximately the same sag, \ang{2.02} versus \ang{2.00}, compared with \ang{7.85} without the reflex. These examples demonstrate transfer of particular reflex responses after calibration, not invariance of all controlled behavior to neural coding. \begin{table}[htbp] \caption{Knee-reflex demonstration, graded baseline versus spiking twin at the matched operating point (5 s runs; settle statistics over the last \qty{2}{\second}).} \label{tab:spike_knee} \small\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.42\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}} \toprule \textbf{Metric} & \textbf{Baseline} & \textbf{Spiking twin} \\ \midrule Knee angle at \qty{0.05}{\second} & \ang{15.79} & \ang{15.79} \\ Settle mean (last \qty{2}{\second}) & \ang{43.5} & \ang{44.4} \\ Settle range & \ang{41.6}--\ang{44.9} & \ang{41.9}--\ang{46.7} \\ Extensor / flexor activation (window means) & 0.53 / 0.53 & 0.58 / 0.56 \\ Antagonist alternation & \qty{0.5}{\hertz}--\qty{2}{\hertz} & \qty{7.4}{\hertz} (dominant peak) \\ Ia interneuron firing at settle & graded, subthreshold & \qty{95}{\hertz}; Ib \qty{0}{\hertz} \\ \bottomrule \end{tabularx} \end{table} \begin{figure}[htbp] \centering \includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{simulink_knee_spiking_twin.pdf} % ALT TEXT: see simulink_knee_spiking_twin_alt.txt beside the figure file. \caption[Simulink knee-reflex twin, baseline versus spiking]{Knee-reflex demonstration at the matched operating point: graded baseline (solid indigo) and spiking variant (dashed orange). Full \qty{5}{\second} run (A) and final \qty{2}{\second} window (B). The spiking response has a slightly wider oscillation band.} \label{fig:spike_knee} \end{figure} \subsection{AnimatLab Conversions} The tested spiking conversions did not preserve the graded models' rhythm (Table~\ref{tab:spike_animatlab}). Converting thresholds while retaining graded synapses preserved near-baseline oscillations, whereas converting synaptic amplitudes and decay changed or eliminated alternation. These results identify the synapse conversion as a limitation of this mapping. They do not demonstrate that a suitably calibrated spiking implementation cannot reproduce the reference behavior. \begin{table}[htbp] \caption{AnimatLab spiking conversions versus their graded baselines (5.1 s headless runs; joint ranges in degrees where the rhythm survives). The thresholds-only ablation converts the neurons but keeps the graded synapses.} \label{tab:spike_animatlab} \small \begin{tabular}{@{}lcc@{}} \toprule \textbf{Variant} & \textbf{Baseline (graded)} & \textbf{Spiking copy} \\ \midrule Two-layer walker & \qty{0.443}{\second} rhythm; & dead (2 spikes; \\ & hip $-15$ to $+23$, knee $-1$ to $+60$ & hip pinned near $+6$) \\ Bilateral variant & \qty{0.462}{\second}; antiphase $-0.42$ cycle & latched; one side at \qty{442}{\hertz}--\qty{450}{\hertz} \\ Reorganized project & latched (tonic drives) & synchronous \qty{11.8}{\hertz} co-bursting; \\ (standalone export) & & same-leg envelopes $r = 1.000$ at lag 0 \\ Thresholds only & \multirow{2}{*The BPA-actuated walker exercised the chain from neural activation through the actuator force model to multi-joint motion. In the supported air-stepping run, the virtual harness carried \qty{70}{\percent} of the \qty{411}{\newton} body weight. The period was \qty{1.542}{\second}, knee RoM was \ang{63.5}, and peak forces were \qty{880}{} and \qty{1372}{\newton}, at a peak pressure of \qty{372}{\kPa}. With split left/right drives and retuned feedback, the W2L robot progressed \qty{1.72}{\meter} over \qty{30}{\second} under the support protocol. It retained progression at \qty{60}{\percent} drive and passed 12 of 12 perturbed reruns, but did not satisfy the strict contact-duty walking criterion; below that drive the gait ceased. The mechanical support was not weaned. In the separate human-model drive-weaning study, the selected score improved from $-161.57$ to $-145.07$, with ten contact cycles per leg and contact duties of 0.71 and 0.65. It passed eight of eight perturbed reruns and retained bilateral stepping down to zero handus, repeatable supported stepping was demonstrated, while harness-free walking was notfive seconds, knee excursions were \ang{1.35} right and \ang{0.95} left, while the vertical rig carried \qty{94.68}{\percent} of body weight and angular stabilization remained active. Disabling muscle forces under the same support settings caused lumbar failure after \qty{0.202}{\second}. This comparison establishes a contribution of the muscle controller under strong assistance, not independent balance. A separate run with rhythmic drive completed its horizon, but alternating gait and progression after settling have not been verified. A subsequent matched 40-second comparison retained the same geometry, initial pose, reference-tension capacities, and external assistance in both conditions. During 15--40 s, vertical assistance supplied 80\% of body weight. The additional control combines muscle-mediated separation feedback (160 N/m, capped at 20 N) with a 6\% activation floor on currently abducting routes, compared with the 5\% global floor (Table~\ref{tab:cad_abductor}). Full recorded trajectories reproduce bit for bit between fresh reference and accelerated runs.
